title: RST1: retained-block sequential shift testing with linear source count

claims.statement: For RST1 in proof.md, for every integer N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, set n=ceil(log2 N), k=n+6 and use exactly the retained-block sequential projective-testing configuration specified there. Unconditional entire-secret recovery has probability at least 49/64>2/3. On every execution branch the same algorithm has total sequential work T=O(N n^2 log2(n+2)^2), hence O(2^n n^2 (log2 n)^2) for n>=2, jointly with the other three resource bounds and clean-input tolerance below. All constants are absolute. The declared supported representative envelope B(n)=2^n n^2 (log2 n)^2 for n>=2 has exact growth index 1. The complete implementation and charged addressing/generation costs are proved in proof.md.

All constants are absolute. The declared supported representative envelope B(n)=n log2 n for n>=2 has exact growth index 0. For RST1 in proof.md, for every integer N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, set n=ceil(log2 N), k=n+6 and use exactly the retained-block sequential projective-testing configuration specified there. Unconditional entire-secret recovery has probability at least 49/64>2/3. On every execution branch the same algorithm has total acquired source count Q=n+6=O(n), jointly with the other three resource bounds and clean-input tolerance below. All constants are absolute. The declared supported representative envelope B(n)=n has exact growth index 0. The complete implementation and charged addressing/generation costs are proved in proof.md.

For the same RST1 algorithm/configuration in proof.md, for every N>=2 and every s, n=ceil(log2 N) and actual acquired count Q=n+6, the guaranteed malformed-copy threshold is tau(n,Q)=0. All Q copies must be independent ideal coset states. Under this promise unconditional full-secret success is at least 49/64 and all four resource bounds hold jointly on every branch. No behavior for malformed copies or impossibility of positive tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed-sample count among Q acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
